entries.test: Comparative studies of unintentional wholesale fabrication by LLMs and humans outside disorder-associated hallucinations would test the asserted contrast.
entries.note: The surrounding text explicitly excludes disorder-associated hallucinations and distinguishes fabrication from jokes and deliberate deception.

entries.test: Public mechanistic studies and controlled experiments could establish whether LLM fabrications arise from erroneous recombination of learned textual elements.
entries.note: The subsequent explanation involving Gary Oswalt is tentative, but this general causal assertion is firm.

entries.test: Research comparing LLM hallucinations with human failures to recall an object's location could establish differences in mechanisms and error patterns.
entries.note: The proposition broadens the specific comparison with forgetting car keys to human errors generally.

entries.test: Controlled studies varying training-data volume and parameter count could test their causal effects on reproduction of training inputs.
entries.note: Here 'can sometimes' describes an asserted demonstrated capability, rather than an uncertain future possibility.

entries.test: The NYT lawsuit's filed exhibits would establish the number of examples, prompt lengths, and extent of reproduced text.
Published training-data extraction studies and reproducible experiments would establish whether neural networks memorize some training material.

entries.note: 'Seriously out of touch' is an evaluative judgment. 'Ignoring' also goes beyond the stated failure to acknowledge the literature.
Reasons to doubt deep understanding do not amount to the explicit likelihood assessment supplied by the drafter. The shallow-understanding attribution is expressly tentative.

entries.test: Public evaluations and controlled interventions on LLM reasoning and world representations could test the asserted limitations and whether superficial understanding causes them.
entries.note: Marcus quotes and explicitly endorses his own words. The proposition omits the vast-dataset framing and the accompanying claim that LLMs approximate well.

entries.test: LeCun's public statements before and around February 2024, compared with Marcus's position, would establish whether his stated position shifted into agreement.
entries.note: The extracted proposition isolates the public-position claim and does not include the separate assertion about Hinton's knowledge.

entries.test: Training-text extraction results and evaluations of the causal reasoning, common sense, and world-model abilities Marcus identifies would test the two assertions.
entries.note: The post supplies concrete capabilities associated with 'deep understanding,' making a substantive test possible.

entries.test: Public evaluations of hallucination patterns and robust common-sense reasoning in contemporary LLMs would test the asserted limitations.
entries.note: This is an empirical interpretation of model failures, rather than merely an insult.

entries.test: A representative survey of classical-AI experts on Hinton's argument, together with evaluations of the disputed LLM capabilities, would test the substantive assertions.
entries.note: The drafter reduces the disputed view to any understanding, although Marcus explicitly allows possible shallow understanding. The assertion about near-universal expert disagreement has factual content.

entries.test: Published extraction demonstrations comparing repeated lengthy model outputs with known training materials would establish the claimed memorization.
Contemporaneous replication results and public documentation of OpenAI's filtering would establish whether the specific example had been blocked by publication.
entries.note: 'Will no doubt by now have' expresses firm confidence about an already-completed action. The drafter weakens it to 'almost certainly' and labels it 'likely.'

entries.test: Repeated training-text extraction experiments across prompts and examples would establish whether reconstruction occurs recurrently rather than as an isolated fluke.
entries.note: 'Certainly can happen' asserts an evidenced capability and recurrence, rather than a probabilistic forecast.
